post.caption: A pomander opened like an orange. The word comes from French for apple of amber. The amber was ambergris, a waxy substance from sperm whales. Its gold or silver case was pierced so the scent could escape. There were often four to eight segments, each with a different scent. One German pomander from the 1500s labels its segments cinnamon and nutmeg. A German gold pendant from the late 1500s carries a tiny cupid. Pomanders hung from a neck chain or a girdle. Wearers believed a good scent helped keep the air healthy. Later the name passed to an orange studded with cloves.
